The ACEPS national registry describes participating fellowship applicants as completing an ACGME-accredited plastic surgery residency by the match-cycle cutoff; Hopkins lists Maryland medical-license eligibility. ABPS certification has its own prerequisite training, practice, examination, and case requirements. A fellowship and this independent course do not confer board eligibility.

boardEligibilityNotice: ABR radiation oncology board eligibility depends on ABR requirements, including eligible clinical year, completion of qualifying accredited radiation oncology training (or approved alternate pathway), examinations, and licensure. Dana-Farber describes its clinical brachytherapy appointment but does not publish detailed applicant rules on the page reviewed. Confirm all requirements with the programme and ABR.

boardStatus: As checked 2026-10-07: CAST publishes skull-base fellowship programme requirements and lists Mass General Brigham among CAST-accredited programme entries. ABNS describes one general neurological-surgery certification pathway and an oral Tumor focus that includes skull-base tumors/endoscopic surgery. It does not publish a separate Skull Base board exam or individual skull-base certificate. NASBS match is administrative selection, distinct from both. No fellowship-specific ABNS exam blueprint or exam weighting was located; course alignment is only to public CAST education requirements and ABNS broad domains, not a formal blueprint.
boardEligibilityNotice: MGB states candidates must have completed or be in their senior year of an ACGME-accredited programme or equivalent in their home country; CAST standards for a CAST-accredited post-residency fellowship require satisfactory completion of an ACGME or foreign-equivalent accredited neurological-surgery residency. A NASBS-listed BWH programme has distinct published match fields and eligibility details; verify directly with each programme. ABNS board eligibility depends on ABNS requirements and the individual’s training/certification trajectory, not on this fellowship or course. Current rules can change. Independent self-study grants no board eligibility, exam credit, licence, fellowship appointment or operative competence.

boardStatus: Nutrition support fellowship is a clinical training track, not itself a standalone ABMS-recognized physician specialty/subspecialty. NBPNS offers a separate physician certification examination (physician nutrition specialist); CNSC is a separate multidisciplinary credential. BWH’s public page expects the fellow to sit the ASPEN CNSC exam. The public ABMS member-board roster does not list clinical nutrition as an ABMS specialty/subspecialty; this does not negate NBPNS’s independent credential. boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course confers no credential and creates no eligibility. NBPNS’s current public exam page requires an active medical license, active ABMS/osteopathic/equivalent primary specialty certification, at least two of its listed nutrition expertise criteria, application/fee and board approval; criteria are reviewed annually. The BWH programme describes post-residency/prior surgical residency eligibility. CNSC and NBPNS are not interchangeable. Verify current rules directly with the boards.

American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN), partner board in BIM certification
boardStatus: ABPMR offers a distinct Brain Injury Medicine subspecialty certification; ABPMR states it has offered the certification in partnership with ABPN since 2014. This is not a primary specialty board and is not an automatic consequence of self-study or of listing a course. The 2026 ABPMR exam outline is the blueprint used here.
boardEligibilityNotice: As checked 2026-10-07, ABPMR says BIM exam applicants need a current, valid, unrestricted medical license and must be ABPMR diplomates in good standing or hold qualifying ABMS-board sports medicine subspecialty certification (ABOS orthopaedic sports medicine is excluded); for post-2022 examinations they must also complete 12 months of an ACGME-accredited BIM fellowship after residency and be recommended by the programme director. Verify current requirements directly with ABPMR/ABPN. This independent curriculum does not confer eligibility.

boardNames: American Board of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (ABPMR) — Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine subspecialty certification
boardStatus: A separate ABPMR PRM subspecialty certification examination exists; the board page lists 280 questions in two 3.5-hour sections and an every-other-year schedule (checked 2026-10-07; next listed exam October 26, 2027). It is distinct from primary PM&R certification. This is a physician fellowship, not a generic directory label, research-only postdoctoral position, or non-physician supplement.
boardEligibilityNotice: ABPMR requires ABPMR diplomate status in good standing, an unrestricted qualifying medical license, and an accepted training route. The usual route is two years of ACGME-accredited PRM fellowship after PM&R residency; ABPMR specifies combined or consecutive-training alternatives. Self-study grants none of these. Hopkins public pages say one or two years depending on prior experience, while 2026 ACGME PRM requirements say 24 months and the KKI application page describes a two-year appointment. Resolve shorter-route details directly with the program and ABPMR; do not assume eligibility.
